population.note: FICTIONAL. About 44M US adults (16.9% of ~262M) are on an incretin for any reason; 23% (~60M) have ever used one. Arithmetic: ever − current = 6.1% of adults (~16M) are used-and-off now. If ~35% of current users are restarters (5.9% of adults) and ~1.5% of adults are off now after at least one earlier restart, then (5.9 + 1.5) / 23 ≈ 32% of ever-users have cycled. That fits the parent's one-year persistence of about a third and a 36–47% restart rate. Age check, weighting bands at 20/33/24/23% of adults: 1.6 + 5.3 + 6.0 + 4.1 = 17.0%. Over-65 use doubled (9→18%) as the Medicare demonstration became permanent-in-practice. Under-30 use rose only slightly (≈6→8%), where the 'unmedicated' identity is strongest. Income: the bottom third climbed fastest from Medicaid opt-ins but still trails at 13%, because the Medicaid states are not the highest-obesity states and prior authorisation is heavier. Off-drug populations: ~16M who stopped, mostly over GI effects, cost or coverage loss at job change. ~38% of adults with obesity have never used a GLP-1, mostly uninsured working-age adults in non-opt-in states and the 18–29 refusers. Children: ~0.4% of under-18s are on a drug (adolescents 12+ mostly); the under-12 off-label share is still skewed to upper-income families.

access.public_coverage: Medicare: the GLP-1 Bridge pilot was not allowed to lapse in Dec 2027. CMS rolled it into a five-year CMMI demonstration (2028–2032) under the same BMI/comorbidity criteria; the beneficiary copay stays $50; Medicare's net price was renegotiated from $245 to $215/month in exchange for formulary placement of next-gen molecules. Part D's statutory weight-loss exclusion is legally intact; coverage runs entirely on demonstration authority. Medicaid: 31 states plus DC have opted into the same $215 rate. Public programmes are now the largest single payer of incretin fills, with ~18.5M of ~44M adult users (42%). Gross public spend: 18.5M × $215 × 12 ≈ $47.7B/yr. Roughly half of it is diabetes-indicated use that was already covered before 2026, so the obesity-specific increment is ~$24B/yr. Retatrutide is not yet on the demonstration formulary (CMS review 2028).
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: generic semaglutide at $6–40/month, now exported widely. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 70–110/month, and US mail-order 'pharmacy tourism' from Canada is tolerated rather than authorised. Brazil, Mexico and much of SE Asia have generics; ~160+ countries have generic access. Generic tirzepatide is not yet available in major markets.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ~44M adult users: public ~42% (18.5M), commercial ~32% (14M), brand cash-pay ~18% (8M), gray market ~8% (3.5M). Managed decline: TrumpRx/LillyDirect/NovoCare cash for injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide stepped down from ~$350 to $199–249; oral starter doses from $149 to $129; maintenance orals $149–199. List prices are unchanged (Wegovy $1,349) and almost nobody pays them. Retatrutide launched Mar 2028 at a $1,249 list price and $499/month via LillyDirect cash. That premium is what powers the gray market: unapproved 'research-grade' retatrutide vials from Chinese API suppliers sell for $120–200/month. Employer coverage fell from 60% to 52%. Many employers cite the public programme as the reason: 'Medicare will pick them up at 65.' Compounding came back through 503A 'personalised dose' scripts (micro-doses and added B12) and offshore peptide sites the FDA cannot reach.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema, approved 2027)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, approved Feb 2028)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: alcohol use disorder, guideline-endorsed (ASAM/APA 2027 guideline: semaglutide as an evidence-supported option, strongest with comorbid obesity); Novo sNDA filed Q4 2027 and under review
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol reduction outside AUD criteria: 'gray-area drinkers' prescribed low-dose semaglutide by telehealth
'quiet dose' / focus / calm microdosing marketed by telehealth wellness brands to people without obesity
pediatric under-12 use under specialist care
nicotine, gambling and compulsive-shopping craving reduction (observational; phase 2 trials for smoking cessation ongoing)
unapproved retatrutide for 'recomp' among gym users before and after approval
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. CagriSema was approved in Jan 2027 (it was under review at the start) and is positioned below tirzepatide on price. Retatrutide's BLA was filed Jan 2027 and approved Feb 2028 under standard review, 13 months after filing. That launch realises the next-gen driver. Its label figure is 28.3% at 80 weeks (up to ~30% at 104 weeks in BMI≥35), with dysesthesia and heart-rate warnings. Survodutide was filed in mid-2027 and is under review, with no decision before late 2028. Amycretin is in phase 3 with no filing and is not on the US market. MariTide (monthly) is in phase 3 and not on the market. Semaglutide's AUD sNDA is pending. Muscle-preserving adjuncts (bimagrumab combinations) are in phase 2/3. Global incretin market ~$110B (2027).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. The triple agonist's higher doses carry higher GI rates at escalation.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; Ozempic 'not recommended in severe gastroparesis' (Jan 2025) carried across class.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Delayed gastric emptying is a known pharmacological effect. Whether it persists after stopping is disputed. MDL 3094 (E.D. Pa.) passed ~24,000 filed claims by mid-2028, mostly gastroparesis and ileus, with pancreatitis and NAION claims in sub-tracks. The first bellwether trials are scheduled for late 2028.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Ileus labelled. Anaesthesia societies' pre-procedure hold guidance is updated. FDA has added no new class warning. Novo and Lilly disclose litigation reserves but have not settled.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss, and higher with triple-agonist magnitudes.
Plaintiffs' expert reports lean on pharmacovigilance disproportionality. Large RCTs still show no confirmed causal increase; absolute risk is low.
Concern sharpened with 28% average loss on retatrutide and with Medicare-age uptake doubling. Geriatricians report falls and frailty anecdotes; no population estimate.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None regulatory. The CMS demonstration 'encourages' resistance-training referral but does not require it.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohorts still conflict; absolute risk is very rare.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA 'very rare' label; no US class label; litigated in an MDL sub-track.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: a 2027 observational registry (n≈40k) found ~10% of users reporting 'reduced enjoyment' at 6 months vs ~5% of matched comparators. It is not trial-quantified and confounded by expectation. The same mechanism underpins the AUD guideline.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None on labels. FDA sent untitled letters to two telehealth brands over 'calm and focus' claims; manufacturers neither claim nor disclaim it.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Trial and real-world figures still conflict. The larger losses on the triple agonist make regain more visible in people who lose coverage.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; the chronic-therapy framing is entrenched in the CMS demonstration criteria.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Signal reinforced in older users with very low intake.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; effects in adolescents; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About six years of rigorous follow-up now exists. Nearly a third of ever-users have cycled, and there are still no cycling-specific outcome data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements on CagriSema and retatrutide.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved incretin product passed ~4,000. Reports include unapproved retatrutide from 'research peptide' vendors: dosing errors, endotoxin contamination, wrong peptide.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning letters, import alerts on API shipments and a final 503B exclusion. Enforcement against offshore sites is largely ineffective.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Seen in retatrutide phase 3; mostly mild and transient.

food_and_beverage.state: GLP-1 households are ~30% of US households. Snack and confectionery volumes are down low single digits annually, sugary drinks more. Protein, fibre and 'small format' SKUs have become standard rather than niche. A countertrend exists: artisanal bread, butter and 'real food' brands court the unmedicated, and some (e.g. regional bakeries, heritage dairy) report growth from that identity.

alcohol.state: US spirits and beer volumes fall for a fourth straight year. The heaviest-drinker decile, the profit core, is visibly thinner as the AUD guideline brings low-dose semaglutide into addiction and primary care. Diageo and Brown-Forman are cutting SKUs, moving into premium low-ABV and non-alc, and lobbying quietly on the AUD sNDA's label scope.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down. Smaller plates, tasting menus and 'half portions' are standard. Bar revenue is the weak line. Communal 'long table' supper clubs flourish in a few cities as a social form of the unmedicated movement.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep closing stores, and Torrid has shrunk its fleet by roughly a fifth. Mainstream brands profit from re-sizing. A small market for deliberately generous cuts has grown around unmedicated aesthetics.

fitness.state: Strength training for muscle preservation is the growth story, sold to older adults through Medicare Advantage gym benefits and to triple-agonist users. Traditional cardio-and-diet weight-loss programmes have mostly folded.

insurance.state: Employers keep retreating (60%→52%) and treat public programmes as the backstop. Pharmacy trend is moderating as net prices fall. Medicare Advantage plans compete on GLP-1 companion benefits. Self-insured firms add 'wait for Medicare' language to benefit decisions for workers in their 60s.

pharma.state: Lilly leads, with tirzepatide, Foundayo and now retatrutide. Novo is defending with CagriSema, the AUD filing and its oral pill. Volume growth outpaces per-unit price erosion. Litigation reserves are a disclosed but manageable line, and ex-US generics compress international margins.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Among over-45s with insurance, thinness reads as 'on it' and is unremarkable. A body that is visibly heavy and healthy-looking now reads two ways: as lack of access, or as a declared choice, the unmedicated signal.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Public coverage has narrowed the gap for the old and the Medicaid poor. The widest gap is now among uninsured and underinsured working-age adults in non-opt-in states, who turn to gray-market vials. Triple-agonist thinness at $499 cash is the new upper-income marker.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Most medicated households eat small, scheduled meals. Among under-30s in Brooklyn, Austin and Portland (OR), 'full table' supper clubs and bread-baking circles make eating to satiety a deliberate public ritual.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Dating apps added an optional 'unmedicated' badge in 2027, used mostly by 20-somethings. Couples counsellors report 'mismatched appetite' as a presenting issue, both for food and for sex, when one partner is on-drug.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite has split into two moral readings: a symptom to be quieted, and evidence of being fully alive. The unmedicated movement is a cross-partisan coalition. MAHA-aligned parents in Texas exurbs who distrust pharma sit beside fat-liberation and slow-food progressives in Brooklyn, and they agree on little else.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: registry estimate of ~10% reporting reduced enjoyment vs ~5% baseline; unquantified in RCTs. Telehealth wellness brands sell low-dose 'quiet' plans (compounded semaglutide at 0.1–0.5 mg weekly, $99–179/month) to an estimated 1.2M people, most without obesity. They are counted within the cash and gray-market user segments.
interior_life.framing: Feature. Wellness marketing names it 'quiet', 'calm' and 'freedom from noise'. Addiction medicine calls the same thing treatment, under the AUD guideline. Critics and the unmedicated movement call it flattening. All three names are in daily use.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Some knowledge-work circles, especially sales and finance in New York and Chicago, talk openly about 'quiet dose' for focus and less impulsive snacking or drinking. Employers neither encourage nor discourage it. Productivity claims are anecdotal, and a few managers privately complain of 'flat' teams.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: There is a small but noted genre of musicians and writers who say they stopped the drug in order to work, and 'off for the album' is a phrase. Hyper-intense flavours, loud music and extreme sports are marketed toward on-drug users seeking a hit of feeling.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Mismatched desire within couples is a recognised complaint. Some users credit reduced compulsion with steadier relationships; others report emotional distance. No population data.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The unmedicated identity is a cultural rather than electoral force. It shows up in MAHA rhetoric against 'drugging appetite' and in left critiques of pharma. Neither has moved legislation this cycle.

state.regulatory_posture: Still pro-access and pro-speed on approvals: CagriSema and retatrutide were approved, and the AUD sNDA is under review. Enforcement against compounders and offshore peptide vendors continues by warning letter and import alert but is visibly outpaced.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. Subsidy works through the extended CMMI Medicare demonstration ($215 net, $50 copay) and Medicaid opt-ins in 31 states plus DC. No new legislation; Part D's statutory exclusion still stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Unchanged: BMI/comorbidity criteria and prior authorisation. No adherence monitoring or benefit conditioning.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The price gap between India/Canada generics ($6–110) and US brands ($129–1,349) is a fixture of political talk. Chinese API vendors supply the US gray market for retatrutide, and US customs seizures are rising but marginal.

events.event: CMS announces that the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot will continue as a 2028–2032 CMMI demonstration. Beneficiary copay stays $50; Lilly and Novo accept $215/month net in exchange for formulary access. 31 states plus DC opt their Medicaid programmes in at the same rate.

ASAM and APA joint guideline names semaglutide an evidence-supported pharmacotherapy for alcohol use disorder, strongest with comorbid obesity. Novo files an AUD sNDA in October; spirits makers cut volume guidance.

GLP-1 products-liability MDL 3094 passes 20,000 filed claims for gastroparesis, ileus and pancreatitis. The court sets the first bellwether trials for late 2028, and Novo and Lilly book litigation reserves.

FDA import alert targets Chinese 'research peptide' exporters after adverse-event reports tied to unapproved retatrutide pass 600. Researchers estimate several hundred thousand Americans are injecting it before approval.

FDA approves Lilly's retatrutide, the first triple agonist, with a label showing 28% mean weight loss and a dysesthesia warning. It launches at $1,249 list and $499 via LillyDirect; Medicare formulary status is pending.

FDA sends untitled letters to two telehealth brands selling 'quiet dose' semaglutide for 'calm, focus and freedom from noise'. The same week, a Brooklyn supper-club network says 40,000 members have signed its 'unmedicated' pledge.

open_tensions: Public programmes are now the default payer for over-65s and Medicaid users, while employers retreat. Coverage still rests on demonstration authority rather than statute, so a CMS reversal or a budget fight could strand ~18M users.
Retatrutide's $499 cash price against $120–200 gray-market vials has rebuilt an unregulated market for the newest molecule, with harms the FDA cannot reach offshore.
Late-2028 MDL bellwether verdicts on gastroparesis and pancreatitis could reprice risk and reshape labels, or collapse the tort, just as use in the over-65s doubles.

Reward blunting is sold as calm, prescribed as addiction treatment and rejected as flattening by a growing unmedicated identity. There is still no trial-grade measure of how common it is or what cycling does to it.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US; brand exclusivity still runs to roughly 2031–32.
Medicare beneficiary copay for covered obesity GLP-1s remains ~$50/month.
Wegovy list price remains $1,349/month, and almost nobody pays it.
Foundayo (orforglipron) remains on the market as a daily oral small-molecule GLP-1.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed in Jan 2026 stays off the Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels, and the effect remains classed as debunked.

prose.headline: Medicare Is Now America's Diet Plan. Retatrutide Is Here, the Vials Are Cheaper, and Brooklyn Is Proudly Eating Bread
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2028, roughly one American adult in six takes an incretin drug, and almost one in four has tried one. The interesting number is the gap. About sixteen million people have used these drugs and are not on them now: they quit over nausea, lost a job and its coverage, or paused and drifted. Nearly a third of everyone who has ever started has stopped and come back at least once. The country is not on the drug so much as moving through it.

The biggest single payer is now the government. Washington did not decide this in one vote. The Medicare Bridge pilot was meant to end in December 2027, but CMS quietly extended it as a five-year demonstration. The manufacturers accepted $215 a month instead of $245 in return for a guaranteed seat at the table. Thirty-one states and DC brought Medicaid in at the same rate. Seniors still pay fifty dollars. Use among people over sixty-five has doubled. Employers are retreating further, and some benefits managers now say openly that workers in their sixties can wait for Medicare. Coverage that rests on demonstration authority rather than law is something everyone in the industry watches.

Prices have stepped down without falling apart. Cash-pay injectables cost around two hundred dollars, and oral starter doses $129. List prices are unchanged, and nobody pays them. Abroad, Indian generics cost what a sandwich does, and Canadian mail-order is tolerated with a wink.

In February the FDA approved retatrutide, Lilly's triple agonist: twenty-eight percent average weight loss, surgical results from a pen. At $499 cash it is the new mark of money. A gray market had grown in anticipation and was already supplying it. Research-peptide vials shipped from Chinese suppliers sell for a hundred and fifty dollars, sometimes containing what the label says. Import alerts and warning letters continue, and the adverse-event count keeps rising.

The courts have caught up with the stomach. The federal products-liability docket in Philadelphia holds more than twenty thousand claims for gastroparesis, bowel obstruction and pancreatitis. Science has not settled whether delayed gastric emptying persists after people stop. The first bellwether juries sit in late 2028, and both companies have booked reserves.

The drugs have also moved into addiction medicine. A 2027 guideline from the addiction psychiatrists made semaglutide a recognised option for alcohol use disorder. Primary-care doctors now prescribe it to heavy drinkers, and the spirits companies' best customers are drinking less. The quieting that helps a drinker is the same quieting other people call flatness. Telehealth brands now sell it outright as calm and focus at a 'quiet dose', ninety-nine dollars a month, to people who were never heavy. The FDA objects to the wording, not the product.

Against all this, a counter-identity has formed: unmedicated. It is youngest and loudest in Brooklyn, Austin and Portland, Oregon, where supper clubs seat forty strangers at long tables and eating until full is a stance. Dating apps offer a badge for it. Its politics are an odd coalition. Exurban Texas parents who distrust pharmaceuticals and big-city fat-liberation activists who distrust diet culture agree that appetite is not a disease and agree on little else. Under-thirties have barely taken up the drugs.

Nothing has collapsed. Snack volumes slip a little every year, plus-size stores keep closing, and gyms sell muscle preservation to retirees. Restaurants serve half portions and sell fewer cocktails. The country looks healthier, and the obesity rate is still falling. What nobody can yet say is what fifteen years of stopping and starting does to a body, or what years of quiet does to a person.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marisol Vega wakes at six in Tucson. She is sixty-six and on Zepbound, fifty dollars at the Walgreens on Grant. Thursday is shot day. She pinches her thigh above the knee where the bruise from last week has faded.

She eats half an egg and drinks the protein shake her doctor's office mails out. The resistance-band class at the Y is full of women her age, all thinner than they were. Nobody mentions it any more.

At noon her daughter Lucía calls from Brooklyn to say she baked eleven loaves for Saturday's table. Lucía is twenty-nine and does not take anything, and says so in a tone Marisol has learned not to answer. 'You should see people eat, Mamá. Really eat.'

Marisol watches the news with the sound low. A lawyer advertises: Stomach paralysis? You may be entitled. She thinks about the winter she couldn't keep soup down, then changes the channel.

At four her son-in-law Dev comes by to fix the swamp cooler. On the counter he sets down a small cardboard box with Chinese characters on the customs slip and asks if he can keep it in her fridge, because his wife doesn't like seeing it. Reta, he says. Hundred sixty a month, versus five hundred. Marisol puts it behind the yogurt.

For dinner she makes Lucía's grandmother's pozole and eats four spoonfuls. It tastes right, she thinks. It tastes like it used to, mostly.

In bed she reads Lucía's photo caption twice: full table, full hearts. She feels nothing in particular, and she notices that.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Over-65 use doubled (9→18%) as the Medicare demonstration became permanent-in-practice.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism/magnitude: the Bridge pilot started July 2026 with ~10% of enrollees newly eligible and BMI/comorbidity criteria. Doubling 65+ use in about 18 months is asserted, not built from eligibility, uptake or supply.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Roughly half of it is diabetes-indicated use that was already covered before 2026, so the obesity-specific increment is ~$24B/yr.
least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: the parent's CBO estimate was ≥$35B added federal spend over 2026–2034 (about $4B/yr). A ~$24B/yr obesity increment is roughly six times that and is not reconciled with it.

magnitude: the parent put pediatric use at ~0.6% of children with obesity, which is roughly 0.1% of all children. 0.4% of all under-18s is a 3–4x jump in two years with no mechanism given, while the note says under-12 use is still rare.

rationale.badness: This is a harder but recognisable society. Gray-market retatrutide with contamination reports, GI litigation, and falls and frailty concerns in the over-65s add harm. The marketed 'quiet dose' and reward-blunting signal (registry ~10% vs ~5%) are poorly measured (epistemic 5). Cohesion takes a mild hit from mismatched appetite in couples and the unmedicated split. Public coverage narrows access gaps for the old and Medicaid poor, but working-age uninsured adults in non-opt-in states are pushed to gray-market vials. Nothing is catastrophic.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visibly realised. Adoption of 16.9% is +5.9pp, price decline is managed, public expansion comes via the CMMI demonstration and 31 Medicaid states, and AUD is guideline-endorsed with an sNDA. The MDL litigation, 28% triple agonist, gray-market retatrutide, 'unmedicated' movement, marketed 'quiet' layer and no state action are all present. mechanism: most chains are shown, such as the $499 vs $120–200 gap driving the gray market and employers citing Medicare. The doubling of 65+ use and the 0.4% pediatric figure are asserted, and the Feb/Mar retatrutide launch dates conflict. magnitude: population, age, income and payer figures reconcile, and the approval timing (retatrutide 13 months after filing) respects the rules. The ~$24B obesity increment is not reconciled with the parent's CBO baseline, and the pediatric jump is large.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Over-65 use doubled (9→18%) as the Medicare demonstration became permanent-in-practice.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude and mechanism: the starting world says only ~10% of enrollees are newly eligible, so doubling 65+ use needs almost all of them on-drug, against a one-year persistence of about a third. The note asserts the doubling and never shows an uptake chain.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The heaviest-drinker decile, the profit core, is visibly thinner as the AUD guideline brings low-dose semaglutide into addiction and primary care.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: a guideline issued in mid-2027, built on one small RCT plus an unapproved indication, is credited with visibly cutting the heaviest drinkers. Medication treatment of AUD starts from very low uptake, and no prescribing or diffusion chain is shown.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Roughly half of it is diabetes-indicated use that was already covered before 2026, so the obesity-specific increment is ~$24B/yr.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: the starting world cites CBO at ≥$35B of added federal spend over 2026–2034 (about $4B/yr), and a ~$24B/yr obesity-only increment is roughly six times that. The candidate does not reconcile the two, and the half-diabetes split is simply asserted.

rationale.badness: The harms are real but not catastrophic. Gastroparesis litigation, a gray market for retatrutide with contamination reports, and lean-mass and frailty worries in a doubled over-65 user base all bear on health. 'Quiet dose' is marketed to non-obese users with only a ~10% vs 5% reduced-enjoyment registry signal, which is an epistemic and autonomy cost. A new split between medicated and unmedicated, and 'mismatched appetite' in couples, add cohesion costs, while coverage dependent on demonstration authority rather than statute leaves a ~18M-user fragility. This is a harder society with new losers, not a dystopia.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visible in fields and events: 503A and offshore gray-market resurgence, a $215 managed-decline price, a Medicare/Medicaid expansion, an AUD guideline and sNDA, MDL 3094, retatrutide at 28%, the unmedicated movement, and 'quiet dose' marketing. The FDA letters and import alerts are continuing enforcement rather than new state action, so nothing contradicts a driver. mechanism: most chains are shown, including the Medicare extension, the gray-market premium at $499 vs $120–200 and the employer retreat. Two are asserted rather than shown: the over-65 doubling and the visible fall in heavy drinkers after one guideline (claims 1 and 2). The MDL growing to 24,000 claims with bellwethers in late 2028 is also fast. magnitude: on-drug 16.9 and ever-used 23 are inside the envelope; the age, income and payer figures sum correctly, as do the 44M user count and the $47.7B product; the cycling arithmetic closes to 32%; retatrutide approval comes 13 months after filing and CagriSema approval was allowed. The 65+ doubling implies near-total uptake of newly eligible people, and the ~$24B/yr increment sits well above the starting CBO figure (claims 1 and 3).

least_plausible_claims.quote: Over-65 use doubled (9→18%) as the Medicare demonstration became permanent-in-practice.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: the 65+ rate doubling in two years rests on a pilot that began in July 2026 and a starting eligible pool of only about 10% of enrollees. No uptake chain is shown (eligibility, prior authorisation, prescriber capacity), so the doubling is asserted.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Retatrutide launched Mar 2028 at a $1,249 list price and $499/month via LillyDirect cash.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: the event log and pipeline_note say FDA approval and launch came in Feb 2028, so the launch date conflicts with the rest of the world state. The gray-market premium story also depends on a launch only weeks old, yet the gray market is already ~3.5M users.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Medicare's net price was renegotiated from $245 to $215/month in exchange for formulary placement of next-gen molecules.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: manufacturers are said to give an $30/month cut for formulary placement that has not happened, since retatrutide is 'not yet on the demonstration formulary (CMS review 2028)'. The price and the quid pro quo are asserted without a bargaining chain.

rationale.badness: A recognisably harder society with new losers, not a collapse. Gastroparesis litigation, thousands of gray-market and contaminated-vial adverse events, older users with lean-mass and frailty concerns, and a gap between uninsured working-age adults and Medicare/Medicaid users are real costs. Reward blunting is marketed as a feature and measured only by a confounded registry, which hurts the epistemic score. Coverage rests on demonstration authority, but access has widened, so the overall score stays mid-range.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is traceable. The adoption delta is 5.9 points (11→16.9), price decline is managed, public coverage expands, the AUD guideline and sNDA are in place, MDL 3094 carries the litigation signal, retatrutide is approved at 28%, the gray market resurges, the unmedicated movement exists, and the personality layer is a marketed feature. The one thin point is that state_action 'none' sits alongside CMS and FDA actions, which are mostly continuations. mechanism: most chains are shown, such as employers leaning on Medicare, the $499 vs $120–200 price gap driving the gray market, and the guideline thinning heavy drinking. Three are weaker: the 65+ doubling (claim 1), the Feb/Mar retatrutide launch mismatch (claim 2), and the $215 trade for a formulary slot not yet granted (claim 3). The under-30 stagnation is also credited to a cultural identity with only a 40,000-member pledge behind it. magnitude: on-drug 16.9, ever-used 23 and the income and age bands are inside the envelope. The age weighting (≈17.0%), payer mix (44M), 18.5M×$215×12≈$47.7B and the cycling arithmetic reconcile. Retatrutide filed Jan 2027 and approved Feb 2028 meets the 12-month rule, and CagriSema was under review at the start. Deductions are the arbitrary 1.5% 'off after restart' input, applying one $215 price to all public users including diabetes fills, and the date inconsistency.
rationale.generativity: The day in the life is concrete: Marisol's Thursday shot, the Walgreens on Grant, the resistance-band class at the Y, a son-in-law storing a vial behind the yogurt, and the daughter's eleven loaves. Social texture adds the unmedicated badge, supper clubs, 'off for the album', mismatched appetite in couples and a lawyer's ad. Many scenes are implied and the characters carry competing stances on the drug.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Over-65 use doubled (9→18%) as the Medicare demonstration became permanent-in-practice.
least_plausible_claims.why: mechanism/magnitude: the Bridge pilot started July 2026 with ~10% of enrollees newly eligible and BMI/comorbidity criteria. Doubling 65+ use in about 18 months is asserted, not built from eligibility, uptake or supply.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Roughly half of it is diabetes-indicated use that was already covered before 2026, so the obesity-specific increment is ~$24B/yr.
least_plausible_claims.why: magnitude: the parent's CBO estimate was ≥$35B added federal spend over 2026–2034 (about $4B/yr). A ~$24B/yr obesity increment is roughly six times that and is not reconciled with it.

magnitude: the parent put pediatric use at ~0.6% of children with obesity, which is roughly 0.1% of all children. 0.4% of all under-18s is a 3–4x jump in two years with no mechanism given, while the note says under-12 use is still rare.

rationale.badness: This is a harder but recognisable society. Gray-market retatrutide with contamination reports, GI litigation, and falls and frailty concerns in the over-65s add harm. The marketed 'quiet dose' and reward-blunting signal (registry ~10% vs ~5%) are poorly measured (epistemic 5). Cohesion takes a mild hit from mismatched appetite in couples and the unmedicated split. Public coverage narrows access gaps for the old and Medicaid poor, but working-age uninsured adults in non-opt-in states are pushed to gray-market vials. Nothing is catastrophic.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: every driver is visibly realised. Adoption of 16.9% is +5.9pp, price decline is managed, public expansion comes via the CMMI demonstration and 31 Medicaid states, and AUD is guideline-endorsed with an sNDA. The MDL litigation, 28% triple agonist, gray-market retatrutide, 'unmedicated' movement, marketed 'quiet' layer and no state action are all present. mechanism: most chains are shown, such as the $499 vs $120–200 gap driving the gray market and employers citing Medicare. The doubling of 65+ use and the 0.4% pediatric figure are asserted, and the Feb/Mar retatrutide launch dates conflict. magnitude: population, age, income and payer figures reconcile, and the approval timing (retatrutide 13 months after filing) respects the rules. The ~$24B obesity increment is not reconciled with the parent's CBO baseline, and the pediatric jump is large.
